title: Compiler tail code
statement: Given a Boolean flag $d$ and a position $p$, the tail code first adds the value in the main-frame stack location to the zero register and stores the result in the designated result register. If $d$ is true, it then subtracts that stack value from zero, branches to position $p+4$ when the difference is negative, and otherwise rejects; the final instruction accepts. If $d$ is false, the code accepts immediately after the initial addition.
caveat: The supplied snippet does not define the register constants or the meaning of the main-frame stack location, so these are described only by their apparent roles.
